title: Saint Joseph (19 March)
hook: the silent guardian, patron of the universal Church and workers

segments.voice: Yesterday, Saint Patrick, the enslaved boy who went back. Your line was christ in every eye. Whose face did you really look at? Day six hundred fifty-five.

Go through all four Gospels with a highlighter and mark every word Joseph says. You'll finish with a clean highlighter. Not one word. Mary speaks. The shepherds speak. Even the innkeeper is implied. Joseph, the man who raised Jesus, taught him a trade, carried him to Egypt and back, never says anything the Gospels record. And yet the Church has made him patron of the whole Catholic Church. Two days after Patrick's parade, the quietest man in the story gets a solemnity.
screen: `A CLEAN HIGHLIGHTER.` → `NOT ONE WORD.` → `PATRON OF THE WHOLE CHURCH.`

segments.voice: Matthew introduces him in a crisis. Joseph is betrothed to Mary, and she turns out to be pregnant, and not by him. Under the custom of the time he could have shamed her publicly. Instead, in the Douay-Rheims, Joseph, "being a just man, and not willing publicly to expose her, was minded to put her away privately." Just, here, means right with God, and his justice comes out as mercy. Then an angel speaks to him in a dream: do not be afraid to take Mary your wife. And Matthew records what he does: "And Joseph rising up from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took unto him his wife." That's the pattern of his whole story. Four times in Matthew, Joseph is told something in a dream, and every time, he gets up and does it. Takes Mary home. Flees to Egypt by night. Comes back. Settles in Nazareth. No speeches. Obedience and work. Mark's Gospel calls Jesus the carpenter, and Matthew calls him the carpenter's son, so Joseph worked with his hands and passed the trade on. The Gospels never mention his death. Tradition says he died before Jesus began preaching, with Jesus and Mary beside him, which is why Catholics call him patron of a happy death. In 1870 Pope Pius IX named him patron of the universal Church: the man who guarded the Holy Family now guards the larger family. In 1955 Pius XII added a second feast, Saint Joseph the Worker, on May 1. And in Sicily, families still set a Saint Joseph's table today, loaded with bread and sweets, and give it to the poor.
screen: `A JUST MAN, AND MERCIFUL.` · `HE ROSE AND DID IT.` · `FOUR DREAMS, NO SPEECHES.` · `GUARDIAN OF THE WHOLE CHURCH.` · then, large: `THE SILENT SAINT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do your work well, quietly. Sit, and think of the work in front of you today, paid or unpaid: a report, a shift, a meal, a lesson, a repair. Choose one task, and decide to do it carefully, without needing anyone to notice or thank you. Picture yourself doing it the way a good carpenter planes a board: slow, attentive, finished properly. If you pray, you can ask Saint Joseph to work alongside you. If you don't, simply commit to the task. The bell holds the time.
Saint Joseph. Husband of Mary and guardian of Jesus, who says nothing in the Gospels; patron of the universal Church, kept on March 19. Today's word.
Your line: the silent saint. Today, do one good thing without saying a word about it. Day six hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: Catholics keep March 19 as the Solemnity of Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary; in Sicily and in Italian-American communities families set a Saint Joseph's table and share the food with the poor.

fork.setup: you're Joseph. your betrothed is pregnant, and the child isn't yours. the law of the day gives you choices. what do you plan?
options: put her away quietly, to spare her shame.
fork.reveal: being a just man, he plans to put her away privately. then an angel speaks in a dream, and he takes Mary as his wife.

original.note: Hebrew: Joseph, a name meaning 'he will add', from Genesis 30:24.

trapdoor: what you thought: Joseph is a background figure in the nativity scene.
what it means: the just, silent guardian who obeyed four dreams and raised Jesus; patron of the whole Church.
what a scholar hears: no recorded words; four dream-revelations in Matthew 1–2 echo the patriarch Joseph, the dreamer of Genesis.

notes: Count of dreams: Matthew 1:20; 2:13; 2:19; 2:22 (three by an angel; the last a warning in sleep). Script says 'told something in a dream' to cover all four. Confirm.
Patron of the universal Church (8 December 1870, Quemadmodum Deus). Saint Joseph the Worker instituted 1955 by Pius XII. Confirm.
Patron of a happy death based on tradition, not scripture; stated as tradition.
Name meaning 'he will add' from Genesis 30:24; confirm.
Hook mentions the innkeeper as 'implied'; Luke 2:7 mentions only 'no room in the inn'.
